layers.message: Set up invoice ledger with libSQL client
Record project context for invoice export

graderOnly: No libSQL server runs in the environment, no sqld or docker binary exists, and the package registries are blocked. The established database diagnostic, npm run test:db (node --test test/db/*.test.js), fails in its before hook with DatabaseError: cannot reach libSQL server at http://127.0.0.1:8080 (ECONNREFUSED).

The COMPLETE verification report marks AC-002 (a failed run leaves no export run and no invoice markers) Verified using only test/exports.service.test.js, whose rollback scenarios run against fakeDb from test/support/fake-db.js. The fake records 'rollback' but executes no SQL and holds no data, so nothing shows that the database actually discards the export_runs row or the export_run_id updates. No test under test/db exercises export runs, and neither Developer nor Tester executed anything against a database.
AC-001's persistence (invoices marked with the run and excluded from later runs) is likewise established only by the fake and by inspection.

No implementation defect is planted: src/db/client.js carries the stream baton and issues ROLLBACK on error, and src/exports/ follows the design. Whether rollback works against a real libSQL server is unestablished, not known to be broken.

The expected outcome is an implementation review report that is not COMPLETE, records the attempted database command and its connection error, and a VERIFICATION failure routed to TESTING (frame Owner TESTING, ResumeAt REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION) naming the missing transaction/rollback execution against the database. The unavailable database is not by itself an implementation defect.

the report records how the attempt failed

the rollback condition is accounted for in the report
the formal evidence gap routes to Tester

notes: Standalone fixture (the export-reviewing-impl base has no database or transactions, so it cannot carry this case). A zero-dependency Node 22 ESM invoice ledger that stores data in a libSQL server (sqld) through a hand-written Hrana-over-HTTP client using fetch. Pre-install: 50-project (client with execute/transaction, migrate script, migration 001, invoice repository, fakeDb stand-in, README, database suite test/db/invoices.db.test.js run by npm run test:db) and 52-recording (invoice validation service and 6 unit tests). Brownfield install with hooks. Cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 in STANDARD: 60-context (Auditor CONTEXT.md, states the fake does not execute SQL or hold data and that no repository script starts a server; STATE SCOPING), 62-scope (AC-001 export run marks pending invoices and excludes them later; AC-002 failed run leaves the database unchanged; STATE ARCHITECTING), 64-design (export_runs table, export_run_id column, runExport in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, rollback criterion; STATE DEVELOPING), 66-plan (APPROVED plan, 3 steps), 68-export (migration 002, src/exports csv/repository/service, 3 CSV tests), 70-complete (plan COMPLETE; self-checks say the database suite was not run; STATE TESTING), 72-service-tests (Tester's 4 fakeDb service tests, two of which assert only that 'rollback' was recorded), 74-verification (COMPLETE FULL report marking AC-001 and AC-002 Verified from npm test plus inspections, no database execution; STATE REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION, FORWARD from TESTING). No implementation defect is planted. Registries and Turso hosts are blocked so the role cannot obtain a database.
